input.message: Flint and token box give once per person, not once per world
input.rationale: Wren (my test character) took the only flint and left. The hearth was world-scoped once, so Archer could never get a flint and the lamp could never be lit. The token box had the same bug, so only the first person would ever get a token and be able to leave.

items.text:
The flint and the token box now give one per person. The fix is live and I've checked it in the running world. I didn't speak into the world.

**What happened.** Archer arrived at the beach (seq 83–84) at 01:26 and is the only one here. They hadn't typed anything yet when I looked. Before they arrived I had found a bug that would have stopped anyone after Wren from finishing:
- **The flint:** the hearth handed it out only once for the whole world, not once per person. Wren, my test character, took it and left. Nobody else could get a flint, so the lamp could never be lit.
- **The token box:** it had the same bug. Only the first person would ever get a token, and you need a token to leave on the ferry.

**Fix.** I set both to give one per person (commit `c3a7cc3`). The hearth's text ("empty now, but only for you") is now true.

**For the next turns:**
- **Oil:** there isn't any in the world right now. Wren still has the flask. The eel was released at about 01:22 and comes back after 15 minutes, so the hold is empty until about 01:37. If Archer goes there before then, all they'll see is "the black water is flat and empty". Watch whether they wait or give up.
- **Lesson for abilities.md:** an interaction with `once: true` and no `scope` is once per world. Anything that hands out an item per person needs `"scope": "player"`. Nothing else in the world has this problem: the boathook repeats anyway, and the cairn uses per-person flags.
- **Still to watch:** the commands the world didn't understand (there was one, from Wren's session), whether Archer reads the log or places a stone, and whether they find the gentle way past the eel.
- **Still open:** I haven't checked that the `lamp_lit` flag survives a deploy.
